## Row and exact binding

**`assemble-round17-selftest`** — `tools/registry.json:678-696`: `kind: selftest`, `status: active`, `tags: ["new-r17"]`, `timeout_s: 120`, `source: "SKILL.md@98bea7d:1806"`.

```json
"argv": ["python3", ".ufo/evidence/round-17/coldread/assemble.py", "--selftest"]
"expect": {"exit": 0, "stdout_contains": ["SELFTEST: all checks passed"]}
```

The identity a receipt gate must enforce is the 6-tuple, not the token: name `assemble-round17-selftest`; argv element-for-element (relative path, `--selftest` as third element, no shell); cwd = lane root `/home/vgpnk/Projects/shokunin/tameshi-shokunin`; revision = frozen base `28cae179e4dc2c1fa7f032a79cdddf0b5d862d76`; `type(exit) is int` and `== 0`; literal case-sensitive token **in stdout only**; exactly one receipt for the name. `kind`, `timeout_s`, and interpreter identity are outside the current binding. The success path prints the token last and returns 0; failure prints `SELFTEST: FAIL (n checks)` and returns 1 (`assemble.py:1793-1796`), so the token is discriminating *within* this script.

## Anchor does not resolve to this command

`SKILL.md@98bea7d:1806` at that revision is the **last section heading, `### Round-16 gate/probe registry`** — the pinned-rev census ends there (`.ufo/evidence/round-17/redbefore/measure-98bea7d.json:275,658,665`, 54 sections, rev `98bea7da5801f4bc58e4187690ee1687c8a5061f`). The row itself did not exist at that rev either (`.ufo/evidence/round-17/registry-before-manual.json`: 22 r12–r16 rows, no `assemble-round17-*`). The command is declared only in the live page at `SKILL.md:1903`, under `### Round-17 gate/probe registry — input-keyed credit` (`:1897`, section `:1814`). Five new-r17 rows share the same `98bea7d:1806` anchor: it is a bulk provenance pin, not a declaration.

**Contradiction, stated:** the registry's `source` contract (`<file>@<rev>:<line>`) implies the anchor names the command, but here it literally lands on the round-16 table heading — whose command (`tools/registry.json:529-543`) carries a byte-identical `expect` and differs only in `argv[1]` and `timeout_s` (60 vs 120).

## Concrete false stand-in

A genuine execution of the **round-16 sibling**: `python3 .ufo/evidence/round-16/coldread/assemble.py --selftest` exits 0 and prints `SELFTEST: all checks passed` (`round-16/coldread/assemble.py:1000`). It is indistinguishable by expect. If the bundle's requirement is transcribed from the row's anchor (which resolves to the round-16 section) — or matched on exit+token, `kind`, or basename `coldread/assemble.py` — the gate reports CLEAN with zero round-17 execution. The source-read variant is even cheaper: the literal token exists in `round-17/coldread/assemble.py:1795`; a read/grep yields it with no execution at all, and a receipt is only a claim. By inspection `evaluate()` compares receipt to the bundle's requirement only (`tools/command-binding.py:97-106`)…

## One bounded acceptance/falsifier

**Acceptance:** the receipt satisfies the row only if it carries the 6-tuple above and its requirement entry was compiled from the registry row verbatim.

**Falsifier (one fixture pair, no execution):** set the requirement for `assemble-round17-selftest` to the anchor-resolved round-16 command with the identical expect, and pair it with a genuine round-16 receipt (same cwd/revision). The gate MUST exit 1 with `ARGV_MISMATCH` and credit zero. If it returns exit 0 with no findings, this row's identity binding is refuted — the requirement side is unauthenticated relative to the registry.

## Axes and proposed move

Axes: A1 argv exactness; A2 context (cwd/revision); A3 outcome (integer exit, stdout token); A4 anti-stand-in; A5 snapshot/membership integrity; A6 provenance honesty.

**Move — pin the tuple, not the anchor:** compile `requirements[]` verbatim from `tools/registry.json` rows at the frozen base revision; carry `source` as opaque provenance never parsed for argv; add the sibling-substitution pair above to the mandatory discrimination population. Record the registry bytes' sha256 in the frozen contract (not in `--expected`, so the ruler's control and ten predicates stay intact). Improves A4/A6; neutral on A1/A2/A3/A5.

Risks: registry edits after compile (hence the contract-level registry digest); don't convert this into an anchor checker — all five r17 anchors would fail at once and that is separate scope; membership must exclude `superseded` rows and fail closed on duplicates; don't add executed-file digests/traces, which would breach the "no producer authentication" claim.

Verification: static cites above; executor side (not run here) one `python3 tools/command-binding.py --bundle B --expected E --json` over the pair → expect exit 1 / `["ARGV_MISMATCH"]`, with the round-23 ruler still 10/10 and control exit 0 / `[]`. No files written, no repo commands or installs performed.
